column3: “On the mouth of Absalom” is rendered “by the intent of Absalom.”
“Set a word to his heart” is rendered “take the report to heart.”
NASB follows the shorter Hebrew text, without the longer Septuagint addition about the watchman’s report.
“Wept a very great weeping” is rendered “wept very bitterly.”
The Hebrew says only “he mourned”; NASB names “David.” “All the days” is rendered “every day.”
The Hebrew has a feminine verb without a stated subject (“it completed”); NASB supplies “the heart of King David longed.” The meaning is uncertain.
